"Amran" (a command): that is, We sent down a command, "from Our presence." Al-Farra' said: it is in the accusative on the sense of: "In it every wise matter is made distinct, a distinguishing, and a command," meaning: We command with the clarifying of that a command. "Indeed We were ever sending [messengers]": Muhammad ﷺ and those prophets before him.

"A mercy from your Lord." Ibn 'Abbas said: a compassion from Me toward My creation, and a blessing upon them by the messengers We sent to them. Al-Zajjaj said: We sent it down on a blessed night as a mercy. "Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them." The people of Kufa read "Rabbi" in the genitive (jarr), as a replacement (radd) for His words "from your Lord," while the others read it in the nominative (raf'), as a replacement for His words "He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." It was also said that it is in the nominative as a new beginning (ibtida'). "If you are people of certainty" that Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth.

"There is no god but Him; He gives life and causes death, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old." "Nay, but they are in doubt" concerning this Qur'an, "playing" (ya'labun): mocking it, heedless of it.

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky brings forth a manifest smoke﴾. The scholars differed concerning this smoke.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from Sufyan: Mansur and al-A'mash related to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: "While a man was narrating in Kinda, he said: 'A smoke will come on the Day of Resurrection and seize the ears and eyes of the hypocrites, and it will seize the believer like the condition of a cold (zukam).' We were frightened, so I went to Ibn Mas'ud, who was reclining. He became angry and sat up and said: 'Whoever knows should speak, and whoever does not know should say: Allah knows best. For part of knowledge is that a person says of what he does not know: I do not know. Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, nor am I of those who pretend﴾ [Sad 38:86]. Indeed, the Quraysh were slow to accept Islam, so the Prophet ﷺ supplicated against them, saying: "O Allah, help me against them with seven [years] like the seven [years] of Yusuf." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 44, verses 28–32:

﴿Thus⦈ Al-Kalbi said: "Thus do I deal with those who disobey Me." ﴿And We made another people inherit them﴾, meaning the Children of Israel.

﴿The heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾. That is because when a believer dies, the heaven and the earth weep for him for forty mornings, whereas these people had no righteous deed that would ascend for them to the heaven, so the heaven weeps for his loss, and they had no righteous trace on the earth, so the earth weeps for him.

Abu Sa'id al-Sharihi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Fanjawi informed us, Abu 'Ali al-Maqri informed us, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili informed us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Basri informed us, Makki ibn Ibrahim informed us, Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi informed us, Yazid al-Raqashi informed me, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no servant except that he has in the heaven two doors: a door from which his provision descends, and a door into which his deed ascends. When he dies, they both miss him and weep over him." And he recited: "The heaven and the earth did not weep for them."

[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir (Tafsir of Surah al-Dukhan) 9/136-137, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it marfu' except through this route, and Musa ibn 'Ubayda and Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi are weak in hadith." Also by Abu Ya'la in his Musnad: 4/157, and by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 8/327. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' 7/105: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in its chain is Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi, who is weak." Ibn Hajar attributed it in al-Matalib al-'Aliya 3/370 to Abu Ya'la with a weak chain. Al-Busiri said: Abu Ya'la narrated it with a weak chain due to the weakness of Yazid al-Raqashi and Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it in abridged form. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur 7/411 to Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya.]]

Ata' said: "The weeping of the heaven is the reddening of its horizons."

Al-Suddi said: "When al-Husayn ibn 'Ali was killed, the heaven wept for him, and its weeping was its redness." [[See: al-Qurtubi 16/141.]]

﴿And they were not given respite﴾: they were not given time, when the punishment seized them, for repentance or for anything else.

﴿And We certainly delivered the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment﴾: the slaying of their sons, the sparing of their women, and the toil in labor.

﴿From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty, among the transgressors. And We certainly chose them﴾, meaning the believers among the Children of Israel, ﴿knowingly﴾ regarding them, ﴿over the worlds﴾, over the peoples of their time.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Abu Bakr al-ʿAbdusi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid ibn Yazid informed us: Sulayman ibn Yusuf informed us: Wahb ibn Jarir informed us: Shu'ba informed us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, fear Allah as He should be feared. [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Sifat Jahannam, chapter: What has been related about the description of the drink of the people of the Fire (7/307-308), and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also by Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter on the description of the Fire, no. (4325) (2/1446); Imam Ahmad (1/301); Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zaman, Kitab al-Ba'th, chapter on the description of Jahannam, no. (2611), p. 649; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (15/246).]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Seize him﴾, meaning it will be said to the guardians (al-zabaniya): seize him, meaning the sinner. ﴿Then drag him﴾. The people of Kufa, Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Amr read it with a kasra on the ta', and the rest read it with a damma. Both are dialects, meaning push him and drive him forward. It is said: ʿataluhu yaʿtiluhu ʿatlan, when he drives him with violence, pushing and pulling. ﴿To the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾, its middle.

﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of the scalding water﴾. Muqatil said: the keeper of the Fire strikes him on the head, splitting his skull to his brain, and then pours into it scalding water whose heat has reached its extreme. [See: al-Qurtubi: 16/150.]

Then it will be said to him: ﴿Taste﴾ this torment, ﴿indeed you﴾. Al-Kisa'i read "anna-ka" with a fatha on the alif, meaning "because you used to say: I am the mighty." Mujahid said: "The gaze is dazzled by their whiteness and the purity of their complexion." أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو سَعِيدٍ الشَّرِيحِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو إِسْحَاقَ الثَّعْلَبِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنِي الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ فَنْجَوَيْهِ، حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عِيسَى مُوسَى بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْخُتَّلِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو هَاشِمٍ الرِّفَاعِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا زَيْدُ بْنُ الْحُبَابِ، حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي خَثْعَمَ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ كَثِيرٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: "مَنْ قَرَأَ حم الدُّخَانِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ أَصْبَحَ يَسْتَغْفِرُ لَهُ سَبْعُونَ أَلْفَ مَلِكٍ" [[أخرجه الترمذي في فضائل القرآن، باب: ما جاء في حم الدخان: ٨ / ١٩٨ وقال: "هذا حديث غريب، لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه، وعمر بن أبي خثعم يضعف. قال محمد: هو منكر" وأخرجه البيهقي في "شعب الإيمان": ٥ / ٤١١-٤١٢، وقال: "وكذلك رواه عمر بن يونس عن عمر بن عبد الله بن أبي خثعم، وعمر بن عبد الله منكر الحديث". وأخرجه ابن عدي في "الكامل": ٥ / ١٧٢٠، وقال الألباني في "ضعيف الجامع الصغير وزيادته": موضوع. وانظر: الكافي الشاف لابن حجر ص (١٤٨-١٤٩) .]]

in gardens and springs, wearing silk and brocade, facing one another. Thus [it is]; and We will wed them to ﴿ḥūr ʿīn﴾ (wide-eyed maidens).

﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ يَلْبَسُونَ مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَقَابِلِينَ كَذَلِكَ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُمْ﴾ أَيْ كَمَا أَكْرَمْنَاهُمْ بِمَا وَصَفْنَا مِنَ الْجَنَّاتِ وَالْعُيُونِ وَاللِّبَاسِ كَذَلِكَ أَكْرَمْنَاهُمْ بِأَنْ زَوَّجْنَاهُمْ، ﴿بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾ أَيْ قَرَنَّاهُمْ بِهِنَّ، لَيْسَ مَنْ عَقْدِ التَّزْوِيجِ، لِأَنَّهُ لَا يُقَالُ: زَوَّجْتُهُ بِامْرَأَةٍ، قَالَ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: جَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَزْوَاجًا لَهُنَّ كَمَا يُزَوِّجُ الْبَعْلُ بِالْبَعْلِ، أَيْ جَعَلْنَاهُمُ اثْنَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ، وَ"الْحُورُ": هُنَّ النِّسَاءُ النَّقِيَّاتُ الْبَيَاضِ. قَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: يَحَارُ فِيهِنَّ الطَّرْفُ مِنْ بَيَاضِهِنَّ وَصَفَاءِ لَوْنِهِنَّ. وَقَالَ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ: "الْحُورُ": هُنَّ شَدِيدَاتُ بَيَاضِ الْأَعْيُنِ الشَّدِيدَاتُ سَوَادِهَا، وَاحِدُهَا أَحْوَرُ، وَالْمَرْأَةُ حَوْرَاءُ، وَ"الْعِينُ" جَمْعُ الْعَيْنَاءِ، وَهِيَ عَظِيمَةُ الْعَيْنَيْنِ.

Thus it was: "as We honoured them with what We have described of the gardens, springs and garments, so too We honoured them by wedding them" [i.e. ﴿and We wed them﴾ is not "marriage contract" in the sense of ʿaqd al-tazwīj (the marriage contract), since one does not say "I married him to a woman"]. Abu ʿUbayda said: "We made them spouses for them, as a husband is paired with a husband," meaning: We made them two by two. "Ḥūr" (wide-eyed maidens) are women of pure whiteness. Mujahid said: "The gaze is dazzled by their whiteness and the purity of their complexion." Abu ʿUbayda also said: "Ḥūr" are those whose eyes are intensely white and intensely black; the singular is aḥwar, the feminine is ḥawrāʾ; and "ʿīn" is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, meaning one with large eyes.

﴿يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِكُلِ فَاكِهَةٍ﴾ اشْتَهَوْهَا، ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ مِنْ نَفَادِهَا وَمِنْ مَضَرَّتِهَا. وَقَالَ قَتَادَةُ: آمَنِينَ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ وَالْأَوْصَابِ وَالشَّيَاطِينِ.

﴿They call for every kind of fruit therein, desiring it, [and they are] secure﴾: secure from its running out and from its harm. Qatada said: "Secure from death, from ailments and from the devils."

﴿لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولَى﴾ أَيْ سِوَى الْمَوْتَةِ الَّتِي ذَاقُوهَا فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَبَعْدَهَا وَضَعَ: "إِلَّا" مَوْضِعَ سِوَى وَبَعْدَ، وَهَذَا كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ [النساء: ٢٢] ، أَيْ سِوَى مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ، وَبَعْدَ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ، وَقِيلَ: إِنَّمَا اسْتَثْنَى الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولَى وَهِيَ فِي الدُّنْيَا مِنْ مَوْتٍ فِي الْجَنَّةِ لِأَنَّ السُّعَدَاءَ حِينَ يَمُوتُونَ يَصِيرُونَ بِلُطْفٍ إِلَى أَسْبَابِ الْجَنَّةِ، يَلْقَوْنَ الرُّوحَ وَالرَّيْحَانَ وَيَرَوْنَ مَنَازِلَهُمْ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، فَكَانَ مَوْتُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا كَأَنَّهُمْ فِي الْجَنَّةِ لِاتِّصَالِهِمْ بِأَسْبَابِهَا وَمُشَاهَدَتِهِمْ إِيَّاهَا.

﴿They do not taste death therein, except the first death﴾: that is, other than the death they tasted in the world, and "illā" (except) is placed here in the sense of "other than" and "after," as in His saying: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ [al-Nisa': 22], meaning other than what has already passed, and after what has already passed. It is also said: the exception of "the first death," which was in the world, from the death in Paradise is because the blessed, when they die, are gently brought to the causes of Paradise; they meet with rest (rawḥ) and sweet basil (rayḥān), and they see their dwellings in Paradise. Thus their death in the world is as if they were in Paradise, because of their connection to its causes and their witnessing of it.

﴿وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ .

﴿And He has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾.

﴿فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ أَيْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ بِهِمْ فَضْلًا مِنْهُ، ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾ .

﴿As a bounty from your Lord﴾: that is, He did this for them as a bounty from Him. ﴿That is the great triumph﴾.

﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ﴾ سَهَّلْنَا الْقُرْآنَ، كِنَايَةً عَنْ غَيْرِ مَذْكُورٍ، ﴿بِلِسَانِكَ﴾ أَيْ عَلَى لِسَانِكَ، ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ يَتَّعِظُونَ.

﴿So indeed We have made it easy﴾: We made the Qur'an easy, the pronoun referring to something not mentioned explicitly. ﴿In your tongue﴾: that is, upon your tongue. ﴿That perhaps they may remember﴾: may take heed.

﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ فَانْتَظِرِ النَّصْرَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ. وَقِيلَ: فَانْتَظِرْ لَهُمُ الْعَذَابَ.

﴿So watch﴾: wait for victory from your Lord. It is also said: wait for punishment for them.

﴿إِنَّهُمْ مُرْتَقِبُونَ﴾

﴿Indeed, they too are watching﴾: awaiting your defeat, as they suppose.
